title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
source: canonical Remove Nth Node From End of List concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is the first node of a singly linked list and an integer n. Remove the n-th node counting from the end of the list (the last node is position 1) and return the first node of the surviving list. n always refers to an existing node.

examples.explanation: Removing the only node leaves an empty list.

hints: Finding the length first works, but the list must then be walked again.
Two pointers separated by n nodes reach the end together: the trailing one stands just before the victim.
Advance the leading pointer n times, then move both until the leader falls off; splice around the trailer. Removing the first node is the special case.
solution: Two pointers one pass: open an n-node gap between them, then advance both until the leader exits. The trailer sits on the victim; splice around it and handle a removed head by returning the second node. O(n) time, O(1) space.
solutionCode:
def remove_nth_from_end(head, n):
    leading = head
    for _ in range(n):
        leading = leading.next
    trailer = head
    previous = None
    while leading is not None:
        previous = trailer
        trailer = trailer.next
        leading = leading.next
    if previous is None:
        return head.next
    previous.next = trailer.next
    return head
bruteForceCode:
def remove_nth_from_end(head, n):
    values = []
    node = head
    while node is not None:
        values.append(node.value)
        node = node.next
    del values[len(values) - n]
    rebuilt = None
    tail = None
    for value in values:
        fresh = ListNode(value)
        if rebuilt is None:
            rebuilt = tail = fresh
        else:
            tail.next = fresh
            tail = fresh
    return rebuilt
